settings.usageLimitAutoContinue: Continue yolo tabs automatically after a usage limit resets
settings.usageLimitAutoContinueHint: Off by default. Applies only to tabs running Control Tower in yolo mode (a Tower that declared --mode yolo, or a Worker dispatched with --mode yolo); other tabs only get a hint. Codex tabs: once the reset time plus the delay below has passed and the screen still shows the limit, BAT types the text below and presses Enter. Claude Code CLI 2.1.234 and later continues on its own after the limit resets, so BAT never types text into Claude tabs: it only shows when the CLI will continue, and presses Enter when the CLI waits on "Press enter to continue" because the computer slept past the reset. Weekly limits (a reset more than 5 h 15 min away), spend caps and credits are only shown. Typing in the tab while BAT waits cancels it; at most 2 automatic continues in a row per tab.
settings.usageLimitContinueTextHint: Typed into Codex tabs before Enter. Default: 繼續
settings.usageLimitContinueDelayHint: 0–60, default 2, so the limit has actually lifted.
settings.batMcpEnabled: BAT MCP (lets the agent in a tab query BAT)
settings.batMcpEnabledHint: On by default. Claude CLI and Codex CLI tabs that BAT starts (new / restored / restarted tabs and Control Tower dispatches) get the read-only "bat" MCP server: the agent can ask which tab it is, list its Workers, read their output and wait for them. Applies to tabs started after the change. Not added when your custom args already pass --mcp-config (Claude) or define mcp_servers.bat (Codex), nor to commands run as typed. Claude CLI tabs also get hooks that tell BAT when claude waits for you (a permission prompt, a question, an MCP dialog: the "blocked" state); not added when your custom args already pass --settings.

claude.v1v2Help:
V1 vs V2 Differences:

[V1 - Query Mode]
• Each message spawns a new CLI process and rebuilds from JSONL
• Cache efficiency ~25% (high token waste)
• Supports: effort, plugins, systemPrompt
• Stable, fully featured

[V2 - Session Mode]
• Persistent session, no process restart between messages
• Cache efficiency ~84% (significant token savings)
• Does NOT yet support: effort, plugins, systemPrompt
• Experimental, may have limitations

V2 is recommended for cost-sensitive or long conversations.

fingerprintTimeout.title: Timed out fetching the TLS fingerprint
fingerprintTimeout.body: The server port accepted the connection but did not finish a TLS handshake within 5 seconds. Another program (possibly this BAT's own remote server) may be using that port, or the BAT server is not responding. Check the service log, then retry.

fingerprintUnreachable.title: Cannot reach the BAT server
fingerprintUnreachable.body: Nothing is listening on the server port. Make sure the BAT server service started successfully (check its log), then retry.

fingerprintHandshakeFailed.title: TLS handshake failed
fingerprintHandshakeFailed.body: The program on the server port did not present a TLS certificate. Make sure the port belongs to the BAT server, then retry.

fingerprintInvalidPort.title: Invalid server port
fingerprintInvalidPort.body: The server port must be a whole number between 1 and 65535. Go back, fix the port, and run the wizard again.

serverBundleUnavailable.title: Could not download the BAT server bundle
serverBundleUnavailable.body: The installer no longer includes the server bundle: BAT downloads it from the server-bundle-v<version> GitHub release the first time a remote is set up. If this computer cannot reach GitHub, choose "Import local tarball…" and pick bat-server-<target>-v<version>.tar.gz together with its .sha256 file (both are assets of that release, copied over by any means), or set the BAT_SERVER_BUNDLE_BASE_URL environment variable to a mirror and restart BAT. The exact target and version are in the details below.

preconditionMissing.title: An earlier step did not finish
preconditionMissing.body: This step needs a result from an earlier step, and it is missing (the earlier step failed or was skipped). Go back and run the earlier step again, or cancel and start the setup over. The details name what is missing.

profileSaveFailed.title: Could not save the remote profile
profileSaveFailed.body: BAT could not save the settings of the new remote profile, and this setup run was undone. Run the wizard again; if it keeps failing, check the BAT log.

connectTestFailed.title: Connection test failed
connectTestFailed.body: BAT could not connect to the BAT server it just set up. Make sure the server is running (check its log), then retry. You can also skip the test and connect later from the profile.

serverBundleInstallFailed.title: Could not install the BAT server bundle
serverBundleInstallFailed.body: BAT has the server bundle, but installing it on the target failed. The details below show the error the target reported (for example a full disk or no write permission). Fix it, then retry.

serverBundleDistributeFailed.title: Could not prepare the BAT server bundle
serverBundleDistributeFailed.body: BAT could not get a server bundle for this target (for example the server architecture could not be detected, or the cached bundle is damaged). The details below show the reason. Retry; if it keeps failing, check the BAT log.

pickDistro.label: Select WSL distro
pickDistro.description: Choose the WSL2 distro that will run the BAT server. If there is only one, it is chosen automatically.

systemdCheck.label: Check systemd availability
systemdCheck.description: Check that systemd is enabled in the distro. The BAT server runs as a systemd service; without it a later step fails.

installBundle.label: Install BAT server bundle
installBundle.description: Get the BAT server for this BAT version (from the local cache or a download from GitHub) and install it in the distro.

writeSystemdUnit.label: Set up and start the server service
writeSystemdUnit.description: Pick a free port, register the BAT server as a user service that starts automatically, and start it.

noDistro.title: No WSL distro installed
noDistro.body: WSL is installed, but no Linux distro is registered yet. In PowerShell run `wsl --install -d Ubuntu-24.04` (or `wsl --list --online` to see other distros), finish the first-run user setup, then retry.

portInUse.title: BAT server port is already in use
portInUse.body: The BAT server inside WSL cannot use this port (EADDRINUSE). In Mirrored networking mode Windows and WSL share localhost, so a port Windows already uses (for example this BAT's own remote server) is unavailable to WSL. Retry picks another port that is free on Windows; if you specified the port, choose a different one.

lingerFailure.title: Could not enable systemd lingering automatically
lingerFailure.body: WSL2 distro restrictions can cause this. Run sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER manually, then retry.

serviceStartTimeout.title: BAT systemd service start timed out
serviceStartTimeout.body: Inside WSL, run `journalctl --user -u bat-server.service -n 50` to see the service start log; lingering not being enabled is a common cause.

notInstalled.title: WSL2 not found
notInstalled.body: Install WSL2 first, then retry. On Windows 11 / 10 22H2 you can run `wsl --install` in PowerShell.

requiresWsl2.title: WSL2 is required
requiresWsl2.body: Every installed distro runs on WSL 1, and BAT needs WSL 2. Convert one in PowerShell with `wsl --set-version <distro> 2` (`wsl -l -v` lists the names), then retry.

homeUnresolved.title: Cannot find the WSL user's home directory
homeUnresolved.body: BAT could not read the home directory of the default user in the WSL distro. Make sure the distro starts normally (open it once in a terminal and finish the user setup), then retry.

unitSnapshotFailed.title: Cannot read the current BAT service
unitSnapshotFailed.body: Before changing the BAT service in {{distro}}, BAT saves its current settings so that cancelling can restore them, and reading them failed. The details below show the error. Retry.

unitWriteFailed.title: Could not write the BAT service file
unitWriteFailed.body: BAT could not write the systemd unit file of the BAT server in the WSL distro. Make sure the distro is running and its disk is not full, then retry.

serviceStartFailed.title: The BAT service did not start
serviceStartFailed.body: systemd could not start the BAT server service in the WSL distro. The details below show the error; for the service log run `journalctl --user -u bat-server.service -n 50` in the distro. Fix it, then retry.

warning.networkNat: WSL is using NAT networking. No change is needed: Windows reaches the BAT server on localhost through WSL's localhostForwarding (on by default). Only if the connection test fails, switch WSL to Mirrored mode or connect with the distro's IP address instead.
warning.networkMirroredPendingRestart: .wslconfig sets networkingMode=mirrored, but WSL is still running in NAT mode — the setting has not taken effect yet. Run `wsl --shutdown` in PowerShell (this stops ALL running WSL distros) and retry. Setup can continue in NAT mode meanwhile.
warning.networkMirroredUnsupported: .wslconfig sets networkingMode=mirrored, but this Windows version does not support Mirrored mode (requires Windows 11 22H2 or later), so WSL fell back to NAT. Setup continues in NAT mode; localhost still works through localhostForwarding.
warning.networkMirroredNotApplied: .wslconfig sets networkingMode=mirrored, but WSL is running in NAT mode. Either the setting has not taken effect yet — run `wsl --shutdown` in PowerShell (this stops ALL running WSL distros) — or this Windows version does not support Mirrored mode (requires Windows 11 22H2 or later). Setup can continue in NAT mode.
warning.networkUnverified: WSL reports networking mode "{{mode}}". BAT has only been verified with NAT and Mirrored, so the connection test may fail in this mode.
warning.connectFailedNat: WSL is in NAT mode and connecting to localhost failed. Check that localhostForwarding is not disabled in .wslconfig, switch WSL to Mirrored mode (then run `wsl --shutdown`), or connect with the distro's IP address instead.
warning.wsl1Only: BAT only supports WSL2. Run `wsl --set-version <distro> 2` before continuing.
warning.systemdDisabled: systemd is not enabled. BAT will fall back to a manual `wsl exec` start command.

warning.containerPortExposed: Container {{name}} publishes the BAT server port on all host interfaces ({{hostIps}}), so other machines on your network can reach it. It was created before BAT bound Docker ports to 127.0.0.1 only. To fix it, run this wizard again with "Create new" (the new container is published on 127.0.0.1 only), then remove the old container yourself with docker rm -f {{name}} once you no longer need its data. BAT will not change or delete it.
warning.containerLegacyImage: Container {{name}} runs a BAT server image built before the Docker networking fix, so the server cannot be reached through the published port. Rebuild the image (npm run build:docker-image) and run this wizard again with "Create new". BAT will not change or delete the old container.
warning.nameTaken: Docker container {{taken}} already exists and was left untouched; BAT will create {{name}} instead.

daemonUnavailable.title: Docker daemon not detected
daemonUnavailable.body: Make sure Docker Desktop is installed and running. Expand the details to see the full error.

portInUse.title: BAT server port is unavailable
portInUse.body: BAT could not publish the BAT server of this container on a free 127.0.0.1 port. For a container BAT is creating, BAT removes it and Retry picks another free port. For an existing container that publishes the port this BAT's own remote server listens on, change the remote server port in Settings, or choose "Create new".

portUnpublished.title: The container does not publish the BAT server port
portUnpublished.body: The existing container does not publish the BAT server port (9876/tcp) on this computer, so BAT cannot connect to it. Choose "Create new", or recreate the container with -p 127.0.0.1:<port>:9876 and retry.

noContainers.title: No Docker containers found
noContainers.body: You chose to use an existing container, but Docker lists no containers on this computer. Retry and choose "Create new", or create a container first.

containerNamesExhausted.title: No free Docker container name
containerNamesExhausted.body: Docker containers {{name}} through {{last}} already exist. Cancel and give the profile another name, or retry and choose "Use existing".

mountsNone.title: No folder selected
mountsNone.body: Choose at least one folder on this computer to mount into the Docker container. Retry to open the folder picker again.

mountsInvalid.title: The selected folder cannot be mounted
mountsInvalid.body: Docker cannot mount one or more of the selected folders into the container. The details below show why. Retry and choose another folder.

inspectFailed.title: Cannot read the Docker container
inspectFailed.body: BAT could not read the details of Docker container {{name}}. Make sure the container still exists and Docker is running, then retry.

containerNotOwned.title: Docker container name already in use
containerNotOwned.body: Docker container {{name}} already exists, and this setup run did not create it. BAT will not reuse or remove it. Go back to choosing the container mode to get another name, or use the existing container.

startFailed.title: Could not start the Docker container
startFailed.body: Docker could not start container {{name}}. The details below show what Docker reported. Fix the problem, then retry.

healthUnavailable.title: Cannot read the container health
healthUnavailable.body: BAT could not read the health status of Docker container {{name}}. The details below show what Docker reported. Retry once Docker is running normally.

containerUnhealthy.title: The Docker container is unhealthy
containerUnhealthy.body: Docker container {{name}} reports unhealthy: the BAT server inside it is not responding. Check the container log (`docker logs {{name}}`), then retry.

healthTimeout.title: The Docker container did not become healthy
healthTimeout.body: Docker container {{name}} did not report healthy within 45 seconds. Check the container log (`docker logs {{name}}`), then retry.

pickContainer.title: Choose Docker container mode
pickContainer.description: Use an existing container or let BAT create and manage a dedicated one.

new.label: Create new
new.description: BAT creates a new container with restart=unless-stopped.

existing.label: Use existing
existing.description: BAT starts an existing container without deleting it on rollback.

configureHost.label: Choose SSH host
configureHost.description: Pick a host from ~/.ssh/config, or enter one by hand. BAT always connects through an SSH tunnel.

verifyAuth.label: Verify SSH authentication
verifyAuth.description: Sign in to the host over SSH and check its operating system and home folder. A host key seen for the first time is accepted automatically.

installBundle.label: Install BAT server bundle (SSH)
installBundle.description: Get the BAT server for the host's platform (from the local cache or a download from GitHub) and install it in ~/.local/bat-server on the host.

startServer.label: Start BAT server
startServer.description: Register the BAT server as a user service (systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS) and start it. It listens only on the host itself.

manualHost.title: Enter SSH host
manualHost.description: Host name or IP address. Add the user and port as user@host or user@host:2222 (port defaults to 22).
manualHost.invalid: Invalid host. Use host, user@host or user@host:port (port 1–65535). Only letters, digits, ".", "_" and "-" are allowed, and no part may start with "-". IPv6 addresses are not supported.

hostInvalid.title: Invalid SSH host
hostInvalid.body: The SSH host or ~/.ssh/config alias may only use letters, digits, ".", "_" and "-", and must not start with "-". Pick another alias, or enter the host manually as host, user@host or user@host:port.

permissionDenied.title: SSH authentication failed
permissionDenied.body: BAT signs in with SSH keys only. Make sure your key is loaded in ssh-agent, or set as IdentityFile for this host in ~/.ssh/config, then check that `ssh <host>` in a terminal logs in without any prompt.

hostEmpty.title: SSH host is required
hostEmpty.body: Pick an alias from ~/.ssh/config or enter the host name manually.

forwardingDenied.title: The SSH server does not allow port forwarding
forwardingDenied.body: BAT reaches the BAT server through an SSH tunnel, but the target's sshd refused to forward it (AllowTcpForwarding). Ask the host's administrator to allow TCP forwarding for this account (AllowTcpForwarding local or yes in sshd_config, including any Match block), reload sshd, then retry.

clientMissing.title: OpenSSH client not found
clientMissing.body: BAT cannot find the OpenSSH client (`ssh`) on this computer. Install it (for example `sudo apt install openssh-client` on Debian / Ubuntu), then retry.
clientMissing.body_win32: BAT cannot find the OpenSSH client (`ssh`) on this computer. Install it from Settings → Apps → Optional features → Add a feature → OpenSSH Client, then retry.
clientMissing.body_darwin: BAT cannot find the OpenSSH client (`ssh`). macOS includes it; run `which ssh` in Terminal to check, then retry.

hostKey.title: SSH host key verification failed
hostKey.body: The SSH host key of this server is unknown or has changed. Run `ssh <host>` once in a terminal and accept the host key (if it changed, first make sure the server really was reinstalled), then retry.

connectTimeout.title: SSH connection timed out
connectTimeout.body: The SSH server did not answer. Check that the host is reachable and that the firewall allows the SSH port (22, or your custom port), then retry.

remotePathInvalid.title: The server path cannot be used
remotePathInvalid.body: The $HOME the server reported must be an absolute path without special characters, and the install path must be absolute or start with ~/. The details show the value BAT received.

unitWriteFailed.title: Could not write the BAT service file
unitWriteFailed.body: BAT could not write the systemd unit file on the server. Likely causes: the disk quota is used up, or `~/.config/systemd/user` is read-only. The details show the server's message.
unitWriteFailed.body_darwin: BAT could not write the launchd plist on the server. Likely causes: the disk quota is used up, or `~/Library/LaunchAgents` is read-only. The details show the server's message.

enableFailed.title: Could not enable the BAT service
enableFailed.body: `loginctl enable-linger` or `systemctl --user enable` failed on the server. Hardened distros need polkit or root for this: run `sudo loginctl enable-linger <user>` on the server, then choose "Already fixed, retry".
enableFailed.body_darwin: `launchctl load -w` failed on the server. Likely causes: another user owns the plist, or System Integrity Protection rejected the load. The details show the server's message.

startCrashed.title: bat-server exited on startup
startCrashed.body: The service was registered, but bat-server exited right after starting. Run `journalctl --user -u bat-server -n 50` over SSH to see why, then retry.
startCrashed.body_darwin: The service was registered, but bat-server exited right after starting. Run `tail -n 50 ~/Library/Logs/com.bat-server.log` over SSH (if logging is set up) to see why, then retry.

verifyFailed.title: Could not confirm that bat-server is running
verifyFailed.body: The service seems to have started, but the check found no listening socket. Run `systemctl --user status bat-server` over SSH to see its state, then retry.
verifyFailed.body_darwin: The service seems to have started, but `pgrep -x bat-server` did not find it. Run `launchctl list | grep com.bat-server` over SSH to see its state, then retry.

tunnelFailed.title: Could not open the SSH tunnel
tunnelFailed.body: BAT checks the server through an SSH port forward, and opening it failed. The details below show what ssh reported. Check the SSH connection, then retry.

fingerprintMismatch.title: Reached a different server
fingerprintMismatch.body: The TLS certificate on the checked port does not belong to the BAT server installed on this host, so the check reached another server (for example this BAT's own remote server). Check the SSH host and the server port, then retry.

pickHost.title: Select SSH host
pickHost.description: Pick an alias from ~/.ssh/config to connect to.

remoteTools.installRequestFailed: Could not start the install in the remote window.

unsupported.no-recipe: No one-click install for this tool.
unsupported.needs-root-no-sudo: Installing needs root, but this account is not root and has no sudo.
unsupported.no-package-manager: No supported package manager was found on the host.
unsupported.manual-only: This can only be installed manually on the host.
unsupported.brew-as-root: Homebrew does not run as root.
unsupported.musl-without-apk: This musl-based host has no apk, so the required libraries cannot be installed.
unsupported.node-musl-source-build: Node.js has no official build for musl-based hosts such as Alpine, so nvm would compile it from source. Install it with the system package manager instead (for example apk add nodejs npm).

integrity.claudeManifestSha256: The installer checks the download against the SHA-256 in the release manifest.
integrity.codexSha256Sums: The installer checks the download against the published SHA-256 sums.
integrity.uvEmbeddedSha256: The installer checks the download against SHA-256 hashes embedded in the script.
integrity.distroRepo: Package signed by the distribution repository.
integrity.ghRepoGpg: Package from the official GitHub CLI repository, verified with its GPG key.
integrity.nvmNodeShasums: The nvm install script is pinned to release {{nvmTag}} (raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm). nvm downloads Node.js from nodejs.org and checks it against the published SHASUMS256.txt.

location.nvmDir: Your home directory (~/.nvm, managed by nvm), no sudo

note.reopenTerminalForPath: Terminal tabs that are already open will not see ~/.local/bin until you open a new one.
note.codexEditsProfile: The Codex installer adds a PATH entry to your shell profile.
note.alpineUseSystemRipgrep: On Alpine, set USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0 in the env section of Claude settings.json so it uses the system ripgrep.
note.rgNeedsEpel: On RHEL-family systems ripgrep is in EPEL; enable EPEL first if the install fails.
note.claudeManualUpdate: Background auto-update is off in BAT remote terminals; use Update here or run claude update.
note.nvmEditsProfile: The nvm installer appends a few lines that load nvm to ~/.bashrc (or ~/.zshrc / ~/.profile); nothing else in the file changes.
note.nvmLoginProfile: BAT also appends a marked block that loads nvm to the profile file bash login shells read (the first of ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, ~/.profile that exists; ~/.profile is created when none does), so non-interactive login shells such as bash -lc find this Node.js too. The block is added only once, and it skips loading when nvm is already loaded; nothing else in the file changes.
note.nvmKeepsSystemNode: A Node.js installed by the system package manager stays installed; shells that load nvm use the nvm version first.
note.nvmReopenTerminal: Terminal tabs that are already open will not see nvm or this Node.js until you open a new one.
note.nvmUpdateMovesDefault: Installs the newest LTS with nvm, reinstalls your global npm packages from the current version, and makes it the default. The previous version stays installed. Nothing changes when you are already on the newest LTS.
